data.long_meaning: In Greek, Alexandria means 'defender of mankind'. It was a common name for cities in the ancient world founded by Alexander the Great. In Christianity, Saint Alexandria is a martyr who was tortured and killed for her faith. The name Alexandria carries the meaning “Defender of mankind” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Alexandria usually hope their child will grow to embody defender of mankind and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Alexandria is a historic city located in Egypt, famously known for its significant role in ancient Mediterranean history due to its foundation by Alexander the Great. Alexandria functioned as the capital city of Egypt under the Hellenistic rulers, and it became a major cultural, intellectual, and artistic center of the Mediterranean world between the 4th century BCE and the 5th century CE. It was renowned for its Library of Alexandria, one of the finest institutions of higher learning in the ancient world. The city was also a melting pot of cultures, with a distinct Greek and Egyptian identity, making it a vibrant cultural center.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, Saint Alexandria is a renowned martyr and virgin who lived during the 4th century CE. She was born in Thessalonica, Greece, and was raised as a Christian by her mother, Theophania. When she was about 14 years old, she was seized by pagan soldiers and subjected to brutal torture for refusing to renounce her faith. Despite the torments, Saint Alexandria remained steadfast, and she eventually died as a martyr, leaving behind a profound impact on the Christian community. Her story is a testament to faith, perseverance, and the triumph of the human spirit over adversity. The name Alexandria has come to embody a sense of fortitude and unwavering commitment in the face of adversity, inspiring many throughout history and continuing to do so today.
